problem: Suppose that $f(x,y)=(x-3)(y+1)^{2}.$ Which of the following shaded areas gives the solution to the inequality $f(x,y)\ge 0?$
worked_solution:
Notice that $f(x,y)$ equals zero when $x=3$ and $y=-1.$ These lines divide the $xy$-plane into four regions, as shown below. Since we have an "or equal to" inequality, we use solid lines to divide the plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/83fcb50be8105d19e044245edd1ad492daad4658ffe4a184ce4bd632dd78e4d4.png)

To determine the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region, we pick four test points, one for each region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/099429ef29700b1eb832aee297b3d237737260a44dd01d6fc516b07710758cce.png)

Next, we calculate the sign of $f(x,y)$ in each region using a sign table:

|  | Test point | $(x-3)$ | $(y+1)^{2}$ | $f(x,y)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Top-Left | $(2,0)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Top-Right | $(4,0)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |
| Bottom-Left | $(2,-2)$ | $-$ | $+$ | $-$ |
| Bottom-Right | $(4,-2)$ | $+$ | $+$ | $+$ |

 

Finally, on our diagram, we shade in the solutions to $f(x,y)\ge 0$ using the *last* column of the table above.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041262/assets/15efb1840d7a41f4600d05dcedc0c2ea5149c85e8bc1b502d62130a7da09d1b8.png)
